sources.publisher: Washington State Department of Social and Health Services, Division of Vocational Rehabilitation
sources.title: 2026-2028 DVR State Plan Update
sources.reporting_period: Uses PY2021-PY2025 measures and current 2026 planning statements

pinpoints.locator: DSHS/DVR Response to WSRC Item 1 — Counselor Change Communication
pinpoints.proposition: DVR reports that high caseloads and staff turnover harmed clear, timely and consistent communication; it reports float VRC coverage, a 48-hour inquiry response standard, and 30-day automatic email replies after staff departure.

pinpoints.locator: Order of Selection — High staff turnover and vacancies
pinpoints.proposition: The final plan states that 37 new VR counselors were hired in the prior year and that 64% of VRC4 staff manage caseloads above 100 customers.

pinpoints.locator: Order of Selection — Case service spending outpacing available funding
pinpoints.proposition: The plan reports case-service expenditures rising from $17.5 million in PY2021 to $27.4 million in PY2024, nearly 57%, and describes a projected $7.5 million FFY2025 funding gap.

pinpoints.locator: Goal Three, Priority One — Progress Made
pinpoints.proposition: The plan reports IPE timeliness increasing from 75.6% in Q4 PY2023 to 81.2% in Q4 PY2024 and continuing to improve in PY2025.

sources.publisher: Washington State Department of Social and Health Services, Division of Vocational Rehabilitation
sources.title: 2024-2027 State Plan Update Draft 2026
sources.reporting_period: Draft update prepared for the 2026 State Plan update cycle

pinpoints.proposition: The draft reports that 40% of VRC4 staff manage caseloads above 100 customers.
The draft reports float VRC coverage, 30-day automatic email replies, documentation of contacts within 10 days, and reinforcement of a 48-hour response standard.
The draft reports case-service expenditures increasing from $17.5 million in PY2021 to $27.4 million in PY2024 and states that 25 new VR counselor positions were added.

The draft personnel table reports 52 VRC3 journey staff employed versus 92 currently needed, 63 VRC4 leads employed versus 62 currently needed, and 150 qualified case-carrying counselors serving 10,300 customers as of Dec. 31, 2025, a stated ratio of 69 customers per counselor.
The draft reports IPE timeliness improving from 75.6% in Q4 PY2023 to 81.2% in Q4 PY2024.

sources.publisher: Washington State Department of Social and Health Services, Division of Vocational Rehabilitation and San Diego State University Interwork Institute
sources.title: Comprehensive Statewide Needs Assessment 2022-2025

pinpoints.proposition: Among 682 respondents, 43.0% reported one counselor, 26.7% two, 15.8% three, 5.7% four, 6.6% more than four, and 2.2% never having a DVR counselor.
Among 664 respondents, 29.5% said reaching their counselor was very easy, 40.2% somewhat easy, 16.4% somewhat difficult, and 13.9% very difficult.
The CSNA summary says 43% had one counselor, 26.7% had two, and 22% had three or more; this summary does not reconcile cleanly with the Table 10 categories.
Among 839 respondents, 93.6% reported being able to access services in their primary language and 6.4% reported they could not.
Recommendations include increasing counselor staffing, considering caseload caps and backfill plans, using triage systems, and considering industry-specialist coaches.

sources.publisher: Washington State Department of Social and Health Services
sources.title: Vocational Rehabilitation Strategic Goals

pinpoints.proposition: Targets included increasing satisfaction with service timeliness from 58% to 62%, increasing timely IPE completion from 80% to 90%, and completing 35% of ADA Action Plan items plus progress on an additional 15% by June 2026.

sources.title: 34 C.F.R. § 361.36 — Ability to serve all eligible individuals; order of selection for services
